feed.title: Handling PQ signatures on the stack

entry.title: Handling PQ signatures on the stack
entry.summary:
Addressing the core issue requires tackling the script’s arbitrary fixed limits and lack of genuine consideration for computational resources. A more effective approach would involve restructuring how scripts account for compute, rather than simply increasing thresholds or patching over existing constraints.
In scenarios where a comprehensive solution such as GSR is considered too extensive, an alternative involves making PQ signatures dependent exclusively on BIP 440. This can be achieved by introducing opcode 0xC2, raising stack limits to allow greater flexibility, and potentially revising the numeric type used in scripts to unsigned big integers. The adoption of unsigned big integers is crucial, as this change cannot be seamlessly incorporated through a soft fork at a later stage.
By implementing these targeted adjustments—introducing new opcodes, expanding stack capabilities, and updating numeric handling—the system would maintain the possibility of restoring certain opcodes in future updates while significantly limiting changes to consensus rules when compared to adopting the full GSR specification. This approach preserves opportunities for future development with a leaner and more controlled expansion of the protocol’s surface area.
